chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had the fast of two consecutive months upon him due to Dhikr (Zihar), so he fasted Dhu al-Qadah. Then Dhu al-Hijjah entered upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should fast Dhu al-Hijjah entirely, except for the days of Tashreeq. He makes them up on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so he will have fasted two consecutive months.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it is not befitting for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three days of Tashreeq which he did not fast. And there is no harm if he fasts a month, then fasts some days from the following month. Then if a reason presents itself to him, he can break it, then make them up after the completion of the two months.'

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.ظِهَارٍ: Zihar (a form of pre-Islamic/early Islamic divorce declaration)

ai.seo_question: How does a man make up for interrupted consecutive fasting days during the days of Tashreeq for Zihar expiation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic nuance of maintaining 'consecutiveness' (ittisal) in the two-month expiation for Zihar by allowing the interruption of the days of Tashreeq, provided the makeup fasts are completed immediately in Muharram. It further distinguishes between a complete break due to illness, which requires restarting the count, and a partial interruption, which preserves the continuity of the obligation. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing strict adherence to ritual purity with practical concessions for valid excuses.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who had the Fasts of two consecutive months upon him regardin Zihaar. So he Fasted Zil-Qaad. The Zil-Hajj entered upon him. Heasws said: ‘He can Fast Zil-Hijja, all of it, except for the days of Al-Tashreek (11th, 12th & 13th). He would make up for it during the beginning of Al-Muharram until he completes the three days. Thus, he would have Fasted two months consecutively’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it is not befitting for him that he approaches his wife until he has made up for the days of Al-Tashreek which he had not Fasted, and there is no problem if he were to Fast a month, then Fast a few days from the months which follows it. Then if a reason presents itself to him, he can cut it, then make up for it from afterwards to complete the two months’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who owes two consecutive months of fasting because of Zihar and fasts the month of Dhu al-Qa’dah, then the month of Dhu al-Hajjah comes. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can fast the whole month of Dhu al-Hajjah except the days of tashriq (11, 12, 13) which he can make its Qada’ (compensatory fast) in the beginning of Muharram to complete three days, and in this way he has fasted two consecutive months.’

He (the Imam) said that it is not proper for him to go near his wife before completing Qada’ (compensatory fast) of the three days of tashriq, which he did not fast. It is not harmful to fast one month and certain days of the following month, and if something happens because of which fasting discontinues he can carry out its Qada’ (compensatory fast) after completing the two months.’”
